purpose: Validation of the transit pipeline against planets whose depths are independently known. These are bright hot Jupiters and sub-Neptunes chosen for signal strength, NOT Earth-2.0 candidates, and they are excluded from the candidate ranking.
systematic_note: Fitted depths run consistently below published values. This is a known systematic of the Savitzky-Golay detrending step, which absorbs a little of the transit even with its window forced to at least three times the transit duration. Depths from this pipeline are approximate and biased slightly low; published limb-darkened values take precedence.

targets.why: The first transiting exoplanet ever detected; bright (Tmag 7.1) with a deep transit.
One of the best-studied hot Jupiters; very bright (Tmag 6.8).
The JWST transmission-spectroscopy benchmark, with 1,625 published spectral points.
Very short period, giving many transits within a single TESS sector.
A well-studied sub-Neptune around an M dwarf; a harder, more realistic test.
